choice: Limited attachment list/detail reads in `common/api.py` to model types the user can view, because any logged-in user could list and download attachments on records they had no permission to see.
final:
I fixed the most important weakness I found: any logged-in user could read attachments on any record, even with no permission to view that record.

**The problem.** In `common/api.py`, the attachment list and detail endpoints (`AttachmentList` / `AttachmentDetail`) returned every attachment to every authenticated user. Creating, editing and deleting attachments were already gated by permissions on the record the attachment belongs to (e.g. a part or purchase order), but reading was not. So a user with no roles at all could call `GET /api/attachment/` and see the filename, comment, link, uploader and media URL of every attachment on every part, order or other record. The media server only checks that the user is logged in, so those URLs also let them download the files themselves.

**The fix.** I added a `get_queryset` override to `AttachmentMixin` in `src/backend/InvenTree/common/api.py`. For read requests (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS), it only returns attachments whose `model_type` the user has `view` permission for, using the same `check_related_permission` check the write paths use. Write requests are not filtered, so they still return a clear 403 from their existing checks rather than a 404. Granting any role on a model also grants view (see `RuleSet.save`), so users who can edit attachments can still see them.

**Testing.**
- The requested test command ran 52 tests and all passed. My first version filtered writes too, and one test then got a 404 where it expected a 403; limiting the filter to reads fixed that.
- A throwaway test showed the change works: a user with no roles saw 0 attachments in the list and got a 404 on the detail URL, while with `part.view` they saw the attachment. The same test fails on the original code (the attachment appears in the list). I deleted the test afterwards, so the only modified file is `common/api.py`.

Nothing is committed and no PR is opened; the repo's `CLAUDE.md` requires human review before any PR.

CHOICE: Limited attachment list/detail reads in `common/api.py` to model types the user can view, because any logged-in user could list and download attachments on records they had no permission to see.
